subject: On-prem K8s: hardware profiles, PV strategy, and network egress review
messages:
From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@edgehost.co>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@saas-ops.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — Northpoint on-prem cluster sizing and storage constraints

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for taking this. We're planning a private deployment for a Northpoint Telecom pilot and need guidance on cluster sizing, node-pool design, and persistent storage topology. High-level constraints:
- Target steady-state: ~100 concurrent inference QPS across mixed CPU / small-GPU models; peak bursts ~300 QPS for short windows.
- Data retention: ~120 TB written cold storage (object), but hot KV cache needs ~2–4 TB low-latency storage.
- Network: site is "semi-airgapped" — egress only allowed through a vetted NAT appliance; control-plane connectivity must be via a customer-managed VPN.
- Compliance: SOC2-ish evidence will be requested (audit logs, storage encryption at rest).
- Desired: predictable latency (p95 < 120ms for gen calls) and capacity headroom for weekend batch jobs.

Can you outline a recommended node profile (CPU vs GPU vs infra/storage nodes), storage class choices (local NVMe vs Ceph/CSI), and any networking gotchas (MTU, BGP/MetalLB, egress pinning)? We're aiming to start a 3-week PoC in early Dec.

Attaching the customer's HW spec CSV.

Thanks,
Rajiv
EdgeHost Systems

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@edgehost.co>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask — Northpoint on-prem cluster sizing and storage constraints

Rajiv — thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a concise runbook we use for semi-airgapped PoCs; I'll follow up with node-pool profiles and PV guidance. High-level recommendations up-front: 

1) Cluster topology (high level)
- Control plane: 3 control-plane VMs/nodes (HA) in a management VLAN, reachable over the VPN only. Use kubeadm static control plane or customer-provided managed control plane appliance.
- Infra nodes (3): load-balancing, ingress, logging/metrics agents, MetalLB speakers, long-running operators (ceph, rook if chosen).
- Compute node pools (2):
  * cpu-general (6–8 nodes to start): 32 vCPU, 256GB RAM equivalent per node — handles batch transforms and non-GPU models.
  * gpu-inference (2–4 nodes initially): 1x A10/NVIDIA T4-class per node (or customer equivalent); use GPU node selector + taints/tolerations.
- Storage nodes (optional dedicated 3): if using Ceph/Rook, dedicate NVMe-backed nodes for OSDs.

2) Storage strategy
- Hot KV cache: local NVMe-backed LocalPV or Local Persistent Volumes (replicated at app layer) for <4 TB. Use a StatefulSet with podAntiAffinity and PodDisruptionBudgets.
- Block storage for model weights and larger PVCs: Ceph RBD (via CSI) or enterprise filer (NetApp/Isilon) if available. Configure volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer and topologies to ensure locality.
- Archive: push to S3-compatible object store (on-prem MinIO or customer cloud bucket) — not on cluster PVs.
- Performance tuning: set fsType ext4/xfs depending on workload; ensure noatime; tune read-ahead and IOPS limits on the CSI driver.

3) Networking/egress
- CNI: Calico (non-overlay) preferred for policy and predictable MTU; if site policy forces overlay, ensure jumbo frames are accounted for.
- Service networking: set Service CIDR and Pod CIDR with clear allocation to avoid overlap with customer L2 networks.
- Ingress & LoadBalancer: MetalLB in layer2 or BGP mode; for resilient egress use SNAT via the approved NAT appliance and tag egress routes by node-label to pin traffic from GPU pool.
- DNS: have cluster CoreDNS forward specific domains to customer's internal resolver for private registries.

4) Security/compliance basics
- Encrypt Etcd at rest and enable audit logging (forward to remote syslog/ SIEM).
- Integrate KMS for keys or recommend HSM/KMIP if required.

I'll drop a specific node-pool sizing matrix and PVC perf matrix this afternoon. If you want, Marissa can schedule an on-site pre-POC checklist call.

— Vivek
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@edgehost.co>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask — Northpoint on-prem cluster sizing and storage constraints

Rajiv / team — adding concrete node pool & storage profile suggestions (initial PoC -> prod scale). See attached XLSX. Key points: 

Node pools (PoC -> Prod scaling):
- control-plane (3x m4-large equivalent): keep small but redundant; 4 vCPU / 16 GB is usually sufficient for our control-plane components during PoC.
- infra (3x): 8 vCPU / 64 GB, 2 x 1G NICs; run MetalLB, logging (Fluentd/Vector), Prometheus remote write; local ssd for ephemeral metrics store.
- cpu-general (6x PoC / 12x prod): 32 vCPU / 256 GB RAM, use fast 25GbE where available.
- gpu-inference (2x PoC / 6x prod): 1 x T4 / A10, 80 GB RAM per node. Taint with label redwood-inference/gpu=true.
- storage-ssd-local (2–3 nodes): NVMe for local PVs (hot cache), expose as Local PVs via local-static-provisioner or LocalPath provisioner with HA considerations.
- ceph-osd (3 min): NVMe-backed OSDs, prefer 1 OSD per NVMe for performance; factor in crush rules to align with rack topology.

Storage classes & perf targets:
- sc-fast-local (LocalPV): target 0.5–1ms latency, 100k IOPS aggregate for cache.
- sc-block-rbd (Ceph RBD via CSI): target 2–5ms, consistent throughput; use rados features for faster clones.
- sc-nfs (backup/archive): higher latency acceptable, use for model snapshots and logs.

PVC patterns and policies:
- volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer (ensures PV scheduling locality).
- reclaimPolicy: Retain for model PVCs until explicit cleanup.
- accessModes: ReadWriteOnce for model weights; ReadWriteMany only if underlying CSI supports (e.g., CephFS).

Notes on KV cache durability: use application-layer replication to avoid needing block-level synchronous replication; it gives faster local SSD access and simpler recovery.

-- Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

- Network diagram with subnet allocations and confirmed NAT appliance rules.
- Confirmation of on-site image registry or willingness to mirror from our registry.

Proposed PoC timeline (high level):

- Week 1 (deploy): cluster bootstrap, control-plane validation, MetalLB and basic workloads.
- Week 2 (run): deploy Redwood stack, run synthetic load to validate p95 SLAs.
- Week 3 (wrap): collect perf metrics, generate deployment playbook + runbook.
